mentions.name: pond.li
mentions.description: This app helps people pursue their long-term interests in a structured way by resurfacing items from their archives and collections, bringing stored material back into the present instead of relying on the daily firehose of new information. It deliberately uses LLMs in roles beyond being chat partners.
mentions.problem: People are pulled into the constant stream of novel information every day rather than reaching more often into their own archives and collections.
mentions.audience: Personal users looking to engage with their own archives and long-term interests rather than constant new information.
mentions.source_excerpt: I've been working on something to help us pursue our long term interests in a reasonably more structured way: https://pond.li. The basic problem/idea motivating it is that it'd be valuable to reach more often into our archives/collections (or have them reach out to the present) than be pulled into the great big, novel firehose of information we're exposed to everyday.

mentions.name: Pond
mentions.description: A web app that makes personal archives of text and other media people engage with more available to the present. Its design centers on human-LLM interaction that preserves meaningful cognitive agency.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm making https://pond.li to try and make our personal archives of text and other media we engage with more available to the present. It's an interesting design space at least, partly because it requires taking a stance on what meaningful/cognitive agency preserving human-LLM interaction looks like
